analysis.evidence: וְאֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת תֶּרַח means “and these are the generations of Terah.” The demonstrative points forward to the genealogy that begins by naming Terah’s sons.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ means “and.” אֵלֶּה is a common plural demonstrative pronoun.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68362:1, 68097:1, 67081:1, 66817:2.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine plural construct, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: generations, the account of what came from someone

analysis.evidence: The marked תֶּרַח names the man whose family the heading introduces. The following clause repeats his name as the subject of הוֹלִיד and identifies Abram, Nahor, and Haran as his sons.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The name completes the construct phrase תּוֹלְדֹת תֶּרַח, “the generations of Terah.”
analysis.sense: The father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

analysis.evidence: After the heading וְאֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת תֶּרַח, the repeated name begins the clause תֶּרַח הוֹלִיד. The three names introduced by אֶת, אֶת, and וְאֶת identify the sons Terah fathered.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal proper noun without a prefix or suffix. This second occurrence of תֶּרַח is the subject of הוֹלִיד.
analysis.sense: The father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

analysis.evidence: Terah is the subject of הוֹלִיד. The direct-object marker אֶת introduces each of the three sons he fathered, Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, third person masculine singular, agreeing with תֶּרַח.
Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.definition: Abram, the earlier name of Abraham, son of Terah.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:26 names Abram among Terah’s sons. Genesis 17:5 gives both forms of his name when God renames him Abraham.

analysis.evidence: In תֶּרַח הוֹלִיד אֶת אַבְרָם, “Terah fathered Abram,” אַבְרָם names the first of the three sons listed, followed by Nahor and Haran.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. The preceding אֶת is a separate direct-object marker.
analysis.sense: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham

analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Terah is the subject of הוֹלִיד (“fathered”). The repeated אֶת marks Abram, Nahor, and Haran as the three sons he fathered.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. The preceding אֶת is a separate direct-object marker.

evidence.note: וְאֶת הָרָן closes the list of sons whom Terah fathered.

article.name: הָרָן
article.summary: Genesis 11:26 names Haran among Terah’s sons, alongside Abram and Nahor. The origin of the name is uncertain.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for הָרָן with the root unassigned.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:26 names Haran as the third son listed after “he fathered.” The verse gives no etymology for his name.

analysis.evidence: The marked הָרָן is the third son named after “Terah fathered,” following Abram and Nahor. The next clause names the same Haran as Lot’s father. The verse gives no etymology for the name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name without a prefix or suffix. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word marking Haran as a direct object of הוֹלִיד.
